hero.title: Software Developer

about.heading: About me
about.body: A software developer who enjoys turning logical ideas into working systems. Through hands-on client project work, I've learned to quickly pick up new tools and adapt to fast-paced environments, and I use Claude Code as an agentic development partner — orchestrating multiple AI agents, automating recurring engineering tasks, and running AI-assisted code and security reviews — to ship full-stack features faster without sacrificing quality.

main.name: Course platform for multiple companies
main.description: A multi-company course platform where each school gets its own URL, teachers manage their own courses, and students scan a QR code to browse a calendar and enrol.
bullets: Built a multi-company course platform: QR-code onboarding, month-calendar enrolment, cross-company time-conflict checks, role-based staff management, Google SSO sign-in, embedded location maps (Leaflet / OpenStreetMap), and a Stripe billing skeleton.

Designed a flexible scheduling engine: weekly runs auto-generate an editable per-session table (individual date/time overrides, add or skip sessions) with a one-click "renew term" flow that carries settings forward.

Developed it end-to-end with an AI-assisted, multi-agent workflow using Claude Code — model routing by task complexity, plan-mode design before implementation, and an autonomous weekly task pipeline that self-verifies (typecheck / build) and commits.

Hardened the backend — per-IP rate limiting, security headers (helmet), JWT fail-fast, user-enumeration protection — and applied AI-driven code & security review to catch and fix an account-impersonation vulnerability in the company-registration flow.

smc.name: SMC Project
smc.description: A customer engagement and routing system integrated with Genesys Cloud to assign communication channels and live agents for chat interactions, auto-replies, and report generation.
bullets: Developed and maintained the Vue.js frontend interface for live agent chat interactions.
Implemented WebSockets on both frontend and backend for real-time chat messaging and system notifications.
Built features for agents to search, view, and log customer profiles and historical data during live interactions.
Configured routing queues with custom trigger conditions and automated actions for chat distribution.
Developed Node.js backend logic to batch-export CSV reports and chat histories, generating download paths based on user authorization.
Created background configuration modules for admins to manage multiple dashboard layouts and UI themes.
Wrote SQL queries and stored procedures in Microsoft SQL Server to handle system data storage and report calculations.

serverIntegration.name: Server Integration Backend
serverIntegration.description: High-performance endpoints connecting directly into the core server database.
bullets: Developed endpoints using Golang to handle high-performance connections directly into the core server database.

otto.name: TDS eDOC Project (OTTO)
otto.description: A specialized document management system built on Tradelink's "Trader Documentation Service" platform for OTTO International (OI). It connects an extensive network of supply chain partners — overseas buyers, sellers and freight forwarders — to facilitate, process and optimize multi-national document exchange and workflow automation.
bullets: Developed and maintained the core modules of the global supply chain system and handled daily production support.
Used JasperReports and XSL-FO to generate standard PDF and XML business documents.
Wrote Cron jobs to handle real-time data sync, automated system housekeeping, and log rotations.
Integrated SFTP workflows to automate document transfers from multinational suppliers and forwarders.
Built a barcode/QR code generation module and implemented logic to format sequential unit codes (prefix + padded zeros + current number) with rollover handling.
Added Regex validators to enforce strict data formatting (e.g. specific lengths and counts for HS Code verification).
Implemented Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to manage user permissions (create, view, edit, delete, lock) across different hierarchy accounts and teams.
Created a document template feature allowing users to save completed forms for faster re-use later.

kiosk.name: CMHK Kiosk Project
kiosk.description: A warehouse management system (WMS) kiosk application developed for China Mobile Hong Kong (CMHK), deployed across 4 kiosk units for cargo registration and automated inventory control.
bullets: Worked closely with internal teams and frontline staff to design and implement features for daily logistics operations.
Used Socket.io to build a real-time notification system, connecting client kiosks (receiving/shipping options) with warehouse staff units via push notifications and sound alerts.
Handled asynchronous status transitions to lock the kiosk UI when a staff member is processing an order, preventing duplicate assignments.
Developed backend verification for scanned QR codes to check order data, formats, and duplicates against the database in real-time.
Implemented an automated quantity check that cross-references scanned items and highlights the frontend UI (e.g. changing to green) when matching.
Generated downloadable PDFs via system-created QR codes upon order completion.
Built a heartbeat mechanism where each kiosk sends its machine ID via sockets every 20 seconds, triggering a red alert UI if a unit goes offline.

tecky.body: 16 weeks of intensive training on building up programming skill sets and acquiring the skills to see my own projects through to completion.

portfolio.heading: Portfolio
portfolio.subheading: Selected work, with screens from the real systems.

schedule-tour.title: This is the running product
schedule-tour.body: A school's public page, live: brand header, embedded map, the month's classes. React, Express and PostgreSQL, built end to end.

schedule-tenancy.title: Every school gets its own address
schedule-tenancy.body: A slug in the URL and a QR code on the flyer are all it takes. One codebase, one database, and every query scoped by company — so no school can reach another's data.

schedule-booking.title: A seat is held, or it isn't
schedule-booking.body: The capacity check runs inside a transaction, the teacher's week updates, and Stripe confirms before anything counts as booked. Same API for student, teacher and admin — different scope.

agents.title: One prompt. A whole team.
agents.body: A dispatcher reads the request, picks one of nine roles, and grades the difficulty — and the grade decides the model. A rename runs on the small one; architecture and security get the big one.

agents-handoff.title: Then it has to pass
agents-handoff.body: Developer hands to tester. Both message files move together or switching language shows raw keys; typecheck and build run before any of it counts as done.

otto-tour.title: A document desk for a supply chain
otto-tour.body: Tradelink's platform, running: folders that hold a whole shipment, a grid you can filter down any column, and twenty-five document types across sea, air, rail and courier. Screens are from the UAT environment, with names replaced.

otto-flow.title: A document nobody re-types
otto-flow.body: It arrives over SFTP, opens from a template, is checked against the other documents in its folder, and leaves as PDF and XML on whichever channel that forwarder uses — six of them, plus email. The status track is what everyone watches.

otto-control.eyebrow: Who may touch it, and what it is called
otto-control.title: Permissions and numbers, by rule
otto-control.body: Rights are granted down an account → team → role tree, so an operator can draft but not delete. Document numbers come from a rule — prefix, zero-padded counter, check digit — and the interesting part is what happens when the counter runs out.

schedule.name: Multi-tenant Course Scheduling Platform
schedule.note: Personal project — runs locally, no public deployment.
schedule.summary: A multi-tenant course platform: every school gets its own URL and QR code, teachers manage courses and rosters from a company dashboard, and students scan once to browse a month calendar and enrol across schools.
highlights: Multi-tenant by company slug (`/c/:slug`), with a per-company QR code students scan to land straight on the enrolment page — no app install.
Scheduling engine turns a weekly recurrence rule into a concrete, editable session table: reschedule, cancel or restore a single session, or override just that session's location.
Cross-company time-conflict checking, enrolment deadlines and capacity limits, all enforced server-side.
Company role tiers (owner / manager / teacher) with an audit trail recording who changed which course, when, and what the old and new values were.
Google OAuth SSO, JWT + bcrypt auth, per-IP rate limiting and security headers; an AI-driven security review caught an account-impersonation hole in company registration.
Whitelisted branding settings (not raw CSS) let each company and teacher theme their own public page.
Built end-to-end with a Claude Code multi-agent workflow — plan-mode design, model routing by task complexity, and an autonomous pipeline that typechecks, builds and commits.

kiosk.name: CMHK Kiosk
kiosk.summary: A warehouse management kiosk application for China Mobile Hong Kong, deployed across 4 kiosk units for cargo registration and automated inventory control.
highlights: Real-time notifications over Socket.io connecting client kiosks with warehouse staff units, including sound alerts.
Asynchronous status transitions lock the kiosk UI while a staff member processes an order, preventing duplicate assignments.

startie.name: Startie
startie.summary: An event display and management platform: create, edit and publish events, choose from multiple event profile templates, and pay through Stripe for priority listing and premium customization features.
highlights: Three auth roles — super admin, event owner and event joiner — with an admin review / approve / reject flow before an event goes public.
Event dashboard covering schedule, activities, descriptions, requirements and FAQ, built on react-hook-form.
Rich text via ckeditor5-react for event descriptions and profile content.
react-timezone-select to keep dates accurate when the backend runs in a different time zone.
Stripe Checkout integration for VIP plans and paid customization features.
Unlimited custom tags, target groups and awards, with automatic prize-pool totals.
Three selectable profile templates plus cover image uploads; per-event reports for visitors, comments and submissions.
Next.js frontend with Recoil for global state, talking to an MVC backend over a RESTful API.
